cinnamon_Readme.pdf: 1 README Multimodal Dataset for Cinnamon Powder Adulteration Detection Using Colorimetry, FTIR Spectroscopy, and RGB Images Version: Version 1.0 1.

Introduction This repository contains a multimodal dataset developed for the detection and quantification of cinnamon powder adulteration using machine learning and artificial intelligence techniques.
The dataset comprises three complementary data modalities: colorimet ric measurements, Fourier Transform Infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy, and RGB images.
cinnamon_Dataset_Description.pdf: 1 Dataset Description Multimodal Dataset for Cinnamon Powder Adulteration Detection Using Colorimetry, FTIR Spectroscopy, and RGB Images 1.

Overview This dataset provides a comprehensive multimodal benchmark for the detection and quantification of cinnamon powder adulteration using three complementary sensing modalities: colorimetric measurements, Fourier Transform Infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy, and RGB images.
The dataset was developed to support research on food authentication, adulteration detection, machine learning, computer vision, spectroscopy, and multimodal artificial intelligence.

cinnamon_Dataset_Description.pdf: Three economically important adulterants were considered: • Peanut shell powder • Walnut shell powder • Wood dust powder Each adulterant was mixed with authentic cinnamon powder at thirteen adulteration levels to simulate realistic adulteration scenarios commonly encountered in commercial spice products.
Adulteration Levels Samples were prepared at thirteen adulteration levels expressed as weight percentage (w/w): 0%, 1%, 2%, 3%, 4%, 6%, 8%, 10%, 12%, 15%, 18%, 21%, and 24%.

cinnamon_Readme.pdf: Data Modalities Colorimetric Data The colorimetric datasets contain six color attributes measured using a HunterLab UltraScan VIS spectro-colorimeter: • L* • a* • b* • Chroma • Hue • Color Index Each record also includes the sample identifier and adulteration category.

Each sample includes: • Sample identifier • 2,523 spectral variables • Adulteration category RGB Image Data The image datasets consist of RGB images acquired under controlled illumination conditions using a Sony α7 III digital camera.
Sample Naming Each sample is assigned a unique identifier that is consistently used across all modalities.
cinnamon_Dataset_Description.pdf: Each sample contains: • Sample identifier • 2,523 spectral variables • Adulteration category 3 The spectra capture chemical variations introduced by different adulterants and can be directly used for machine learning, chemometric analysis, and spectral feature extraction.
Sample Naming Convention Each sample is assigned a unique identifier.

Examples: • CP10S25 – Peanut shell powder, 10% adulteration, Sample 25 • CW12S08 – Walnut shell powder, 12% adulteration, Sample 8 • CD24S50 – Wood dust powder, 24% adulteration, Sample 50 where • CP = Peanut Shell Powder • CW = Walnut Shell Powder • CD = Wood Dust • S = Sample number The same sample identifier is consistently maintained across all three modalities to facilitate multimodal data integration.

cinnamon_Dataset_Description.pdf: Data Quality Assurance Prior to publication, the complete dataset underwent systematic validation to ensure data integrity and consistency.

The verification process included: • Validation of sample naming conventions • Duplicate sample detection • Verification of adulteration labels • Confirmation of folder organization • Verification of image filenames • Consistency checking between sample identifiers and category labels • Verification that each adulteration level contains exactly 50 samples The validation confirmed that all 5,850 records are complete, correctly labelled, and internally consistent.
